name: False doctrine
about: False gospels, false prophets and false churches.

teachings.title: Trent's anathema on faith alone
teachings.summary: The Council of Trent's curse on justification by faith alone puts the Catholic Church against the Bible, which teaches salvation by grace through faith without works.
teachings.text:
The Council of Trent, on salvation by faith alone:

CANON IX.-If any one saith, that by faith alone the impious is justified; in such wise as to mean, that nothing else is required to co-operate in order to the obtaining the grace of Justification, and that it is not in any way necessary, that he be prepared and disposed by the movement of his own will; let him be anathema

CANON XII.-If any one saith, that justifying faith is nothing else but confidence in the divine mercy which remits sins for Christ’s sake; or, that this confidence alone is that whereby we are justified; let him be anathema.

The Bible is anathema to the Catholic Church. Jesus Christ Himself, and Paul, Peter, James, all heretics and anathema to them.

**John 5:24**
*Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life.*

**Romans 11:6**
*And if by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace. But if it be of works, then is it no more grace: otherwise work is no more work.*

**Romans 3:20**
*Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin.*

**Ephesians 2:8**
 *For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God.*

**John 3:16**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.*

teachings.title: Loving the truth and hating every false way
teachings.summary: David's psalms of trust are models of prayer that Christ Himself quoted, and loving God's truth, a gift of the Spirit, means hating false prophets who teach damnable heresy while loving those they mislead enough to tell them the truth.
teachings.text:
**Luke 23:46**
*And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.*

David's Psalms of trust in the Lord God, to be delivered and never ashamed, redeemed in His righteousness, are models of prayer, and Jesus upon the cross quotes them (or rather, they quote Him). How much more should we?

The cries to listen to our prayers and save us out of trouble, acknowledging that He is our rock and our fortress, our Savior, our ready help in time of tribulation, they echo through time and are as relevant to Christians today as they were to the King of Israel, and the congregation that sang them 3,000 years ago.

*Into thine hand I commit my spirit: thou hast redeemed me, O LORD God of truth.*

Trusting the God of truth to keep His word, having faith in His promises, is the foundation for our Christian life. Relying on His word to feed us with truth. Knowing the truth that sets us free.

And loving the truth puts us in a position where we hate those that lie about the Lord.

**Psalm 119:104**
*Through thy precepts I get understanding: therefore I hate every false way.*

This love of the truth and understanding of His word is a gift of the Spirit of God.

**1 John 4:6**
*We are of God: he that knoweth God heareth us; he that is not of God heareth not us. Hereby know we the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.*

All things are made known to us by the Spirit, through Christ who is the way, the truth, the light.

And so we should be vexed by false prophets who teach damnable heresy.

**1 Timothy 4:1–2**
*Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils; Speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron*

These false prophets are reprobates concerning the faith. Their lies make their followers twofold more the child of Hell than themselves. They are enemies of God, and we should hate them with a perfect hatred, while loving those misled by them enough to proclaim the truth.

teachings.title: Predestinated in Christ, not chosen to believe
teachings.summary: Predestination in Ephesians 1 and Romans 8 is in Christ, not God choosing who will believe, since God will have all men to be saved and draws all men, so Calvinism and limited atonement are doctrines of devils rooted in pride.
teachings.text:
**Ephesians 1:3-6**
*Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ: According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will, To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved*.

So what is this that is predestined? The saved? Or Christ Jesus by whom we are saved?

Calvinists read this and **Romans 8**, and place the emphasis on themselves, rather than Christ, and so, they claim, that God picks who will believe. This doctrine of devils, like all false gospels, is based on putting themselves before the Lord. Just as works salvation is predicated on the person's own righteousness, not Christ's, the special boy doctrine makes it that they are the elect, not of Jesus perfect work, the lamb slain before the foundation of the world, that all who believe on Him will be saved, but by God's "sovereign will."

But we know that God's will is not for a chosen few.

**1 Timothy 2:3-4**
*For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour; Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth.*

If God exerted His sovereign will, we would all be saved.

As Jesus says,

*And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

Every one.

Limited atonement is a doctrine of devils. It is based on pride.

So we know that all who believe are predestinated in Christ that they will have eternal life, sealed by the Spirit, and if they walk in tha Spirit, will be conformed to the use of God, that we may become separated, to be servants of the Gospel.

And so continuing the theme of Romans 8, the context of which is the works of the Spirit.

That while we are yet in the flesh, knowing the day of redemption will free us from that wretched state, that the Spirit helps heal our infirmities that led us to sin and conforms us to His will, so long as we walk after the Spirit, not feeding the flesh with the things of this world. That the Spirit within us acts also as an intercessor to bring our needs before the Father, so that His will be done in us.

And so, the good news;

*And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.*

Who is called? Who is drawn to faith in God's promise?

**John 12:32-33**
*And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me. This he said, signifying what death he should die.*

All men. But few will answer this call, and seek to be transformed to fulfill His intended purpose for us. The harvest is great but the laborers few. Strait is the gate and narrow the way and few there be that find it. Every name of every person born of water upon this earth is in the book of life. But their names are stricken from it when they die in sin, unbelieving. (Or reprobates, twice-dead)

No where in the Bible do we see names added, only erased. God's foreknowledge, knowing of the end from the beginning, means He knows who will answer the call. It doesn't mean He selects them.

teachings.title: Peace, peace, when there is no peace
teachings.summary: False prophets preach peace, prosperity and a pre-tribulation escape to itching ears, but true preachers warn of judgment and call men to repent and find peace only in Christ.
teachings.text:
**Jeremiah 6:13-15**
*For from the least of them even unto the greatest of them every one is given to covetousness; and from the prophet even unto the priest every one dealeth falsely. They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace. Were they ashamed when they had committed abomination? nay, they were not at all ashamed, neither could they blush: therefore they shall fall among them that fall: at the time that I visit them they shall be cast down, saith the Lord.*

**1 Thessalonians 5:1-3**
*But of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you. For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night. For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape.*

False prophets, claiming to speak the words of God, come with soothing words of peace. Peace with God, despite the sins of the people. Peace with the land, despite the blood of innocents. Peace with those who practice Idolatry and wickedness, in ecumenicalism.

They preach prosperity and health to people with itching ears.

**2 Timothy 4:3-4**
*For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears; and they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables.*

Today, many false prophets also claim that believers won't see tribulation, but rather will be spared destruction, raptured before it begins.

But what does Jeremiah say to Hannah? *The prophets that have been before me and before thee of old prophesied both against many countries, and against great kingdoms, of war, and of evil, and of pestilence.*

Prophets who come with the word of God preach destruction and repentance.

And, in like manner, today we have the word of God, and we are called to do the same.

**Jude 1:22-23**
*And of some have compassion, making a difference: and others save with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh.*

We preach the acceptable year of the Lord. That judgment is coming to every man, and Hell with it. To repent towards God and faith in His Son for deliverance. That man cannot know peace except in Christ. These are the word of God given us in scripture with the command to love one another, to set at liberty from the bonds of the law. To reconcile man with God before it's too late.

**Matthew 11:28-30**
*Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.*

teachings.title: Mystery Babylon, the mother of harlots
teachings.summary: The great whore on seven hills is Rome and its apostate church, with the false religions sprung from her as harlot daughters, drunk with the blood of the saints she martyred in a trail of blood, until the beast and his kingdom make war with the Lamb and are overcome.
teachings.text:
The Whore, Mystery Babylon the Great. Mother of harlots and abominations. Drunken with the blood of the saints she martyred. The golden cup filled of her filthy fornication and abominations.

*That great city which reigneth over the kings of the earth*.

Sitting upon 7 mountains.
Given power by kings to rule.
Decked in purple and scarlet, gold and precious stones and pearls.

Sitting upon many waters, which are peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues.

Who is this great whore? This mother of harlots? This city on 7 mountains, that sits on many waters? Who has martyred the saints of Jesus and committed fornication and blasphemy and other abominations against God?

The city on seven hills is Rome. Its whore, the false religion and apostate church of the Roman Catholics. The harlot daughters all the other false religions that have sprung from it. The Orthodox and the Protestant. All those calling themselves Christ's, professing themselves to be holy and true. But drunk in her fornications. Idolatry. Blasphemy. The abominations of her golden cup. The power of her political control, given by the kings that committed adultery with her. The murder of millions of believers, in a trail of blood, as this empire of mirey clay and iron has conquered much of the earth.

In the end, the 7th empire as described by Daniel (we will look at Daniel 7 tomorrow, along with the destruction of Babylon), will give the beast power to reign and will promote the worship of the beast who was, is not and is again. The fatal wound and Satan bringing the antichrist back to life as the man of perdition, and installing him as the head of the final one world government and religion for a short space.

*These shall make war with the Lamb, and the Lamb shall overcome them: for he is Lord of lords, and King of kings: and they that are with him are called, and chosen, and faithful.*

teachings.title: Study to shew thyself approved
teachings.summary: Paul's writings are scripture that the unlearned wrest to their destruction, so believers must study and rightly divide the word, comparing scripture with scripture, to guard against false doctrine.
teachings.text:
You can see how Paul builds an argument block by block, in one long thought that establishes the foundation of the idea he wants to convey. It is careful and methodical and of the Spirit in its simplicity, but confounding those who don't believe with its dense structure, making his writings a snare for those who don't actually hold the faith that he uses as the foundations for his epistles. Something that Peter addresses in his own epistle to the churches of Asia:

**2 Peter 3:13-17**
*Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness. Wherefore, beloved, seeing that ye look for such things, be diligent that ye may be found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless. And account that the longsuffering of our Lord is salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you; As also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things; in which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction.Ye therefore, beloved, seeing ye know these things before, beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness.*

Peter both acknowledges Paul's standing as an Apostle, his writings as scripture, and that what he writes confounds the unlearned and unstable, the babe in Christ or the unbelieving. Peter appeals to them, saying since they have the faith, they should beware being taken by those who wrest with scripture out of ignorance or unbelief, by false doctrines pulled from the complexity of Paul's writings, as well as scripture in general.

As Paul writes in **2 Timothy 2:15**
*Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.*

We study scripture for God's approval, and to not be ashamed, that is taken astray, caught off guard by an argument we don't have an answer for, being misled by those who wrestle with scripture to pull out false doctrines, etc. To be like the Thessalonians;

**Acts 17:11**
*These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.*

**1 Corinthians 2:13**
*Which things also we speak, not in the words which man's wisdom teacheth, but which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual.*

This is how we grow in grace and peace. This is how we protect ourselves from false doctrines or doubtful disputations by the unlearned and unstable, and the false prophets bringing another gospel. This is how we please God. This is how we can stand stedfast on our faith not being ashamed by naysayers or mockers. This is how we share our faith to others that they may receive the same forgiveness and grace that we have.

So, as we study to be approved by God, it is important to get how the Spirit leads Paul to build his case, his outline for the theology that comes from our salvation. The implications for living in the faith that we share.

teachings.title: Easy-believism and the strait gate
teachings.summary: Salvation by believing on Christ alone, mocked as easy-believism, is the strait gate few find, because pride, works and the false hope of repent-of-your-sins preachers keep men from simply trusting that Jesus paid it all.
teachings.text:
**John 3:16-18**
*For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.*

**Acts 16:30-31**
*And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved? And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.*

This is the Gospel of faith, taught throughout the Bible. But it is derisively called "easy-believism" by those seeking to bring another gospel of works and self-righteousness.

If believing the Gospel for salvation were "easy," then why do so many people struggle with trusting in Christ Jesus alone for their salvation? Why does every false religion reject this simple faith for works and penance?

**Matthew 7:13-14**
*Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.*

Believing on Christ alone for salvation is the narrow way. The strait gate. And there really are few who find it.

Pride and vanity and inability to trust the word of God keeps people from letting go and trusting by faith. They want reassurance that it "worked" before they can let go. They are carrying so much of a burden, and yoked by the law, that they cannot fit through that strait gate. Like a camel trying to pass through the eye of a needle. And so they seek a wider path to their own destruction.

Or they want to force their way through by exhibiting signs of deserving it through their own acts of righteousness, which the Bible calls filthy rags. Greasing the entrance by their own good intentions, so that they can accept that they "deserve" to enter. Not realizing none deserve it, but we are given entrance through Christ.

They want to know without trust, so that they may believe, and so they never can come to the knowledge of the truth. Because *faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen*. And without visible evidence, they doubt, and are given false hope from the "Repent-of-your-sins" types who claim that they may know they are saved if they do certain acts, and behave a certain way. But that false hope gives way when any weight is put upon it, because their standards are impossible to achieve in the flesh. It is impossible to pass through that gate carrying our own works, which are wood, hay and stubble, fit to be burned.

We don't begin to be sanctified until we are in the kingdom already. Until we have passed through that gate. Without faith, it is impossible to please God.

So don't be fooled. Salvation is easy, from a works standpoint because it doesn't require any effort from us to believe that Jesus paid it all. But it is hard from a human standpoint, letting go of all the burdens that keep us from passing through.

teachings.title: Job and the hedge of protection
teachings.summary: Job shows that both wealth and affliction are to God's glory, refuting both the idea that only the wicked prosper and the prosperity gospel, while Satan, the god of this world, works only within what God allows.
teachings.text:
Now God knows who Satan is and what he does and His pointing out Job is deliberate, and in so many ways this is done for our admonition, upon whom the end of the world has come.

If a man as upright and perfect in his ways can be sorely tempted by the persecution of Satan against him, If the hedge of protection may be lifted, to show the glory of God for such a man as job, how can we expect the small tragedies that befall us as believers to be any less to His glory?

If the Book of Job was one chapter, the lesson is present and clear. But as we'll see, there is so many more lessons to learn than simple perseverance in faith.

Satan of course credits the hedge of protection God has placed around Job and his family and the blessings of the holdings that he's acquired which are gifts of God, as the only reason Job's faith is so strong. He says to God that if He put forth His hand now and touched all that he had, Job would curse Him to his face.

I have seen an error among people similar to this, that says only the wicked prosper. Job shows this isn't the case and that wealth in itself is not a bad thing, but that all we have is a gift of God.

Then there's the prosperity Gospel types, who falsely say that if you're not successful and you're not succeeding, that you're not right with God.

But here we humbly learn that whether we are blessed or cursed, all is to His glory. As Paul writes:

**Philippians 4:12**
*I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need*.

Whether you're in good times or bad times or the mix most of us find ourselves in, it's all to the glory of God. His grace is sufficient.

Now the Lord says to Satan, *behold all that he hath is in thy power* but bars him from doing harm to Job physically.

The prime interpretation of this is that God has granted Satan special permission to afflict Job, And that is a fair reading of the text, especially in light of the hedge of protection Satan says God has placed about Job. But, as I've mentioned, the Bible says that Satan is the god of this world, That he is the prince of the power of the air, ruler of this world. Not as God, but as having influence and power over the things of this Earth.

So is the Lord reminding Satan, or enabling him? It's difficult to say. But we should keep it in mind always.

**Ephesians 6:12**
*For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.*

But regardless, Satan is given the power to affect all that Job has, if not his person. And in one day, he does his worst.

First we see that his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine and in the eldest brother's house, this detail is given before the rest, creating tension in the reader.

Then the messengers begin to arrive. One tells of the oxen and asses killed by marauding Sabeans, who are from the south, where modern Yemen is.

Then another arrives to say that the fire of God reigned from Heaven on the sheep in the servants and consumed them.

When God gave permission to Satan to do what he will, he gave him access to the fire of God that rains from Heaven.

**Revelation 13:11-13**
*And I beheld another beast coming up out of the earth; and he had two horns like a lamb, and he spake as a dragon. And he exerciseth all the power of the first beast before him, and causeth the earth and them which dwell therein to worship the first beast, whose deadly wound was healed. And he doeth great wonders, so that he maketh fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men*

The false prophet of the Antichrist will have this power and ability, And it will cause the unsaved to worship the beast and his image.

teachings.title: Honour thy parents, not the tradition of men
teachings.summary: Jesus upheld the commandment to honor father and mother against the Pharisees' Corban tradition, and a generation that abandoned its parents to the state and its children to schools has broken God's multigenerational family order and reaped suffering.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 15:1-9**
*Then came to Jesus scribes and Pharisees, which were of Jerusalem, saying, Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread. But he answered and said unto them, Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition? For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death. But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free. Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition. Ye hypocrites, well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying, This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.*

Here Jesus reinforces the concept of honoring your father and mother, referencing the honor due them, and placing the command against cursing your parents as the direct counterpoint to the 5th Commandment.

**Leviticus 20:9**
*For every one that curseth his father or his mother shall be surely put to death: he hath cursed his father or his mother; his blood shall be upon him.*

The promise of a long life upon the earth for those that honor their parents, versus the death that those who fail to, who rob their parents, deserve.

The doctrine of the Pharisees held that a son who pledged his wealth to the temple, while yet holding on to it for his own use, could declare it as a gift, and exempt the person from their duty to their father and mother.

**Mark 7:11**
*But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free.*

This commandment of men made God's law to no effect. Creating a holier than thou excuse.

The curse of God upon a people who dishonor their parents, leading them to destruction, Is something that we have seen in modern times.

The baby boomer generation was the first to abandon the care and support of their parents to the state. To nursing homes. To their health insurance and Medicare. Food stamps. They also abandoned care of their children to schools and day cares. They broke the generational cycle God had put into place and we have all suffered for it.

They took the inheritance of their parents and squandered it while bragging that they're spending their grandchildren's inheritance on frivolous things.

It's fitting that many have broken relationships with their now dead parents, and their children and grandchildren. And sadly, they spend their final days alone in the same nursing homes they consigned their own parents to.

God put in place a system of family, of fathers in a hierarchy, wives in respectful submission to their husband, children under both, and honor due to the elders, to the widow indeed. A multi-generational family where children are arrows in the quiver of the father. Where each generation provides something to the unit, and stability to society.

But those that have broken this tradition the same is a companion of the destroyer. They've brought only suffering and death.

teachings.title: Righteousness from the God of our salvation
teachings.summary: Believers are made clean by God's imputed righteousness received by faith, not by their own works, and Roman Catholicism's denial of imputation at the Council of Trent is a lie.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 24** is a meditation on the truth of the Christ, the Lord, King of Hosts. Creator of all things, and the truth of the way of righteousness for those that trust in Him.

The gospel message of the Psalms, sung in the Temple, performed by the chief musicians and the congregation is the inspired doctrines of God, and the focus is entirely Jesus.

They may have looked through a glass darkly, but the concepts of Christ are hammered home, in verse after verse, chorus and stanzas of praise for the name of God, the Holy One, the Lord.

Here in the 24th Psalm, David asks *Who shall ascend into the hill of the LORD? or who shall stand in his holy place?*

Those with clean hands and pure hearts, who hasn't put their trust in vanity or lying lips, but who trusted the God of their salvation.

*He shall receive the blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God of his salvation.*

We are made clean of our sins, our hearts purified by the imputed righteousness of God. We receive these blessings by grace through faith, and access to the Kingdom, not by our own righteousness but by submitting to the righteousness that is God's.

**Romans 4:5–8**
*But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. Even as David also describeth the blessedness of the man, unto whom God imputeth righteousness without works, Saying, Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom the Lord will not impute sin.*

There are false religions that deny the imputation of righteousness by faith in Christ. They say that imputation is not taught in scripture. This is a lie.

**2 Corinthians 5:21**
*For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.*

Our righteousness is as a filthy rag, our works could never justify us before a holy and perfect God. But these men believing vanity, and swearing deceitfully, teach that man needs to establish their own righteousness through works of the law, and many are misled by this lie.

**Romans 10:2–4**
*For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge. For they being ignorant of God’s righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.*

Roman Catholicsm rejects the idea that we are made righteous by receiving righteousness from the God of our salvation. The Council of Trent (Canon 11 on Justification) anathematized the idea that people are justified “by the sole imputation of the justice of Christ, or by the sole remission of sins” and that righteousness is "infused" by works, sacraments and "grace transforming a person," so that their own righteousness is established, rather than submitting to the righteousness of God.

But let God be true, and every man a liar. The generation of them that seek His face shall not be ashamed. All who come to the saving knowledge of Christ are made pure, in Him. Righteous, in Him.

**Titus 3:5–7**
*Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost; Which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Saviour; That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.*

The truth of imputed righteousness of God being given the believer is found throughout scripture. And thank God for His grace and mercy. That our sins are washed clean, justified by the blood, and remembered no more.

teachings.title: Pray to God against them that persecute us
teachings.summary: Believers may pray as David did for deliverance and against enemies who seek their hurt, asking God to send His angels to defend them, but must pray only to God and never to angels as false teachers lead people to do.
teachings.text:
**Psalm 35** is a model of prayer that carries with it both the plea for deliverance, and imprecatory, or negative prayers against enemies who seek our hurt.

In David's case, we understand that he was falsely accused, had enemies trying to literally kill him and destroy him.

We may not have the threat against our lives, but we can relate.

The Lord is our Judge of judges. We go boldly before the throne of grace, asking anything, that we may plead our cause. Asking God to get involved in our lives, to fight our fights.

We have such an awesome advocate in Christ Jesus and a Father Whose mercy and judgement is righteous and true. It is foolishness not to go before Him in prayer, knowing that He seeks our prosperity. Not the riches and accumulations of things, as the false teachers preach, but our overall benefit and success spiritually, that we may do His will.

So, of course when we have enemies in this life that seek our hurt, it would be natural that we get God involved.

*Draw out also the spear, and stop the way against them that persecute me*. That is to form a flank before us, a hedge of protection, like a wall of men, spear extended. A host to shield us from the advances against us. To show us and comfort us with the truth that He is our salvation.

Let our enemies be confounded and confused. Let them be scattered as the chaff. Let the angel of the Lord be our guardian. His children have guardian angels;

**Hebrews 1:14**
*Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?*

We can call upon Him to give them direction to not only shield us, but it persecute them that seek to do us harm.

But we shouldn't misunderstand that these ministering spirits are ours to control, or to plea to them. Many pray directly to angels, or archangels, which is wicked.

**Revelation 22:8–9**
*And I John saw these things, and heard them. And when I had heard and seen, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel which shewed me these things. Then saith he unto me, See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book: worship God.*

We pray, as David did, to the Living God. He directs His hosts.

The Bible says that false teachers will mislead people into worshiping angels.

**Colossians 2:18**
*Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind*.

Pray directly to God in all things. Pray for Him to dispatch His angels to defend us and attack our enemies, as David demonstrates here.
